primary.title: Tao Te Ching
primary.author: Laozi
primary.rationale: The foundational text of Taoism, traditionally attributed to Laozi. It is widely available in numerous translations and editions.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to the Tao te ching
secondary.author: Michael Puett and Jade Starr
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive collection of essays by leading scholars offering diverse perspectives on the Tao Te Ching, its historical context, and its philosophical significance.

secondary.title: Lao Tzu and the Tao-te ching
secondary.author: Julian Pas
secondary.rationale: An in-depth academic study that examines the historical and philosophical aspects of Lao Tzu and the Tao-te ching, providing critical analysis.

secondary.title: The Tao Te Ching: A New Translation and Commentary
secondary.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
secondary.rationale: While a translation, Le Guin's extensive commentary provides significant scholarly insight into the text's meaning, context, and enduring influence.

suggestions.notes: Laozi is a semi-legendary figure, and the authorship and exact dating of the Tao Te Ching are subjects of scholarly debate. Primary source availability is high due to the text's antiquity and importance.
